newsitem.title: USA: Travolta's "Michael" lands at top of U.S. box office.
newsitem.headline: Travolta's "Michael" lands at top of U.S. box office.

text.p: John Travolta's winning streak with moviegoers continued over the weekend as he landed at the top of the box office playing a cheeky angel in "Michael," according to studio estimates.

The dark comedy, which also stars Andie MacDowell and William Hurt, earned an estimated $17.8 million during the Friday to Sunday weekend. Since opening on Christmas Day, the movie has earned $27.93 million, making it the best Christmas opening ever.
The movie was produced by the now-defunct Turner Pictures, and released by New Line Cinema, both units of Time Warner Inc.. It averaged $8,313 from 2,141 screens, the highest tally in the top 10.

"Evita," starring pop-star Madonna, also re-wrote history books as it earned $200,000 from two screens. The musical was produced by Cinergi Pictures Entertainment Inc., and distributed in the United States by Walt Disney Co..

Other Oscar contenders doing well in limited release included the Australian drama "Shine," which earned $1.6 million from 207 screens, and "The People Vs. Larry Flynt," which earned $528,000 from 16 screens in its first weekend. Also, New Zealand director Jane Campion's "Portrait of a Lady" earned $105,550 from seven screens.
"Shine" is released by Time Warner-owned Fine Line Features, "The People Vs. Larry Flynt" by Sony Corp.'s Columbia Pictures and "Portrait of a Lady" by PolyGram NV's Gramercy Pictures.

Among the major releases, Tom Cruise's romantic comedy "Jerry Maguire" remained in second for the weekend with an estimated $14.3 million. Its three-week total now stands at $60.6 million. The movie is released by Sony's TriStar banner.
Disney's "101 Dalmatians" held in third with $11.8 million, and has now grossed $104.5 million since opening on Nov. 27.

Last weekend's surprise No. 1, "Beavis and Butt-head Do America," slid to fourth with $10.4 million. The animated road movie's two-week total stands at $41.3 million. The movie is released by Paramount Pictures, a unit of Viacom Inc.

Paramount released the only other new entry in the top 10, "The Evening Star," which opened in 10th with a dim $3.3 million, or per-screen average of $2,632. The sequel to "Terms of Endearment" was roundly panned by critics.
